newsitem.title: USA: Small profit seen should Excedrin win migraine ok.
newsitem.headline: Small profit seen should Excedrin win migraine ok.

text.p: Analysts predicted Bristol-Myers Squibb would derive little additional revenue should the U.S. Food and Drug Administration allow Excedrin Extra-Strength to be marketed for migraine headache pain.

An FDA advisory panel earlier Tuesday voted unanimously that the over-the-counter drug was effective for temporary relief of migraine headaches. The FDA is not bound by its panel's advice, but usually follows it.

Excedrin E-S, sold since 1978, is the third biggest pain reliever in the United States. Bristol-Myers had argued that since migraine suffers treat themselves, an over-the-counter designation was appropriate.

"I wouldn't expect an approval to have any noticeable impact on earnings," said Rodman & Renshaw drug analyst Mario Corso. "I imagine it's already being used for migraines even without the FDA's approval."
He estimated the company had total annual sales of about $1 billion from over-the-counter products, adding, "I'd be surprised if Excedrin sold over $100 million."
"It's not a large market by any means," Corso said, compared with Bristol-Myers prescription products such as Pravachol -- its cholesterol-lowering drug with sales of $1.1 billion in 1996.
But Mehta and Isaly analyst Steve Lisi said a migraine designation for Excedrin would help the company keep its market share in the over the counter market.
"As far as earnings expectations, it won't be important, but it would be positive for their OTC business," he said.
"Success feeds on itself in the over-the-counter market and the more products they have the more they can push their brand name," Lisi said.
